speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a fever and altered mental status starting two days ago; to begin our assessment, how old are you and do you have any underlying medical conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The combination of fever, altered mental status, and a history of haloperidol use for tics is highly suggestive of this condition. I will proceed with checking vital signs for muscle rigidity and requesting blood work to assess for leukocytosis and elevated creatine kinase (CK). REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, CK.
